summary: Iter-75 (backend-only): Cashfree Auto Refund wiring into 2-of-5 OTP refund approval chain. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iter75_cashfree_refund.py (16 tests) → 16/16 PASS. Covers all 6 unit scenarios (monkeypatched cashfree_service.create_refund + payment_service.create_refund, direct _trigger_gateway_refund calls) + full E2E API chain over HTTP with a synthetic paid yacht booking + fake CF order id (real Cashfree production API rejects gracefully as designed).
critical_code_review_comments: refund_approval_routes.py L469-527 _refund_via_cashfree — reads fresh cashfree_refunded_total/cashfree_refund_ids from db before each attempt (resumable ✓), iterates paid cashfree_orders sorted by paid_at asc, caps per-order refund at (order.amount - refunded_amount), decrements a local `remaining` counter, on any failure breaks out and writes gateway_refund_status=failed with gateway_refund_error preserved but withholds gateway_refund_id → idempotent on retry (verified in scenario 3). On full completion, joins refund_ids with ', ' as gateway_refund_id, sets gateway_refund_status=processed and updates all 3 booking collections with cashfree_refund_ids array. Solid.

refund_approval_routes.py L530-555 _trigger_gateway_refund routing — first checks fresh gateway_refund_id (short-circuit 'already_refunded' idempotency ✓), then razorpay_payment_id from booking OR payment_orders (razorpay priority preserved ✓), else calls _refund_via_cashfree, else writes pending_gateway/no_payment_id transaction and returns no_payment_id (manual queue). Order of precedence matches spec.

refund_approval_routes.py L662-668 approve endpoint — gateway-aware success message via gw.get('gateway')=='cashfree' branch. Retry-gateway (L397-412) also gateway-aware. UX text now reads 'Cashfree refund successful' vs 'Razorpay refund successful' correctly.

MINOR (non-blocking): _refund_via_cashfree updates db.cashfree_orders via {id: o['id']} — assumes cashfree_orders documents always have an 'id' field. If ingestion path elsewhere ever inserts without 'id' (only cashfree_order_id), the $inc would silently miss. Confirmed our seeded docs use 'id' UUID and tests pass, but a compound match on cashfree_order_id would be more defensive.

MINOR (non-blocking): _refund_via_cashfree does NOT re-check whether individual per-order refund_ids are already logged if the same request is retried after a partial success where the DB update succeeded but the loop later crashed mid-iteration on a different order — because remaining is recomputed from cashfree_refunded_total each run, this is safe in practice, but each retry does not skip a specific order that already reached full cap (it uses cap = amount - refunded_amount so cap<=0 is skipped ✓). Good.

cashfree_service.create_refund L286-341 — real API mode when configured; production keys currently set in backend/.env (CASHFREE_MODE=production). Our E2E uses a fake CF_FAKE_* order id so the real API returns 4xx and the wrapper returns {success:False,error:<body>}, which _refund_via_cashfree correctly propagates as reason. No real money spent in tests. Confirmed by successful E2E run.
seed_data_creation: PART A unit tests: 6 synthetic bookings/refund_requests/cashfree_orders inserted then cleaned up in the same test (booking_number prefix TEST_CFR-*). PART B E2E: 1 synthetic paid yacht vertical_booking (TEST_CFE2E_*, ₹5000, start_date 2028-12-31, customer_id=customer@airyatra.co.in) + 1 fake cashfree_orders doc (order id CF_FAKE_*) seeded, walked through customer-cancel → OTP request → finance approve → OTP request → admin approve (triggers real Cashfree API → fails as expected on fake order) → appears in /refunds/failed-gateway → retry-gateway (fails) → mark-processed (closes out) → cleaned up in module teardown. No real-money bookings touched.
